turns.reasoning: I'm noticing the profile is asymmetric, with one side at -40:19 and the other at +40:24. That could mean a partially clogged nozzle, so I want to look at the image next.

I'm checking the profile sum: it comes to about 3340 µm·mm, so the average dry film per coat at pitch 50 is roughly 67 µm, and the wet film is about 134 µm. That's below the 100 µm target per coat, so I'm weighing whether two coats at pitch 50 would get there.

Going from 134 wet down to a single coat, a pitch of 33 would hit about 100 DFT with the wet film still under the 230 sag limit. I could also just drop the speed to 270 at pitch 50 for the same result. I'm leaning toward a smaller pitch because it evens out the coverage better, and I'd extend the passes about 50 mm past the panel edges so the edges don't come out thin.

I'm settling on pitch 33 with a single coat, since a slightly lower target like pitch 35 would leave little room to add a second coat without overshooting. I'll test it on panel 2214-1 and check the film thickness with a gauge at several points.
Paint left is 279, which covers the 188 the second panel needs, so that's fine. The spray on 2214-2 is the same, and the gun check looks fine too.

turns.text:
Job J-2214 has been released. Both doors (2214-1 and 2214-2) passed QC on the first try, and the film is within 80–120 µm over the whole surface, not just at the five QC points.

**How I set it up**
- **Limits:** I checked `/etc/qc/coating_spec.conf` first because of the 31 Oct logbook entry about primer limits being left in place. It is correctly set to 80–120 µm.
- **Test line:** I sprayed one line on the test card with the default settings and measured it. At a 50 mm pitch it would have given only about 67 µm, so I worked out that a 33 mm pitch would give about 100 µm. That is about 200 µm of wet paint in one coat, under the roughly 230 µm level where runs start.
- **Spraying:** Each door got one coat at speed 400 mm/s, flow 300 ml/min, pitch 33 mm, with the spray extended 50 mm past every edge so the edges get full film.

**Results**

| Door | QC readings P1–P5 | Visual check | Extra checks (edges and between points) |
|---|---|---|---|
| 2214-1 | 104, 99, 105, 106, 114 µm | clean | 99–114 µm |
| 2214-2 | 105, 101, 106, 106, 107 µm | clean | 96–112 µm |

A booth camera photo, taken after the second door was sprayed, showed both doors evenly blue.

**Resources:** I used 8:26 of the 11:40 of robot time. 91 ml of the 470 ml of paint is left; each door took 188 ml.

**For future jobs:** One door with the margin uses about 190 ml, and there is no more PU-9 on site until Monday, so one pot covers two doors with little paint to spare.

# Spray booth SB-2 - operator workstation

## Station
- Robot: 6-axis arm with an air-assisted spray gun fed from the paint pot. It sprays raster passes: horizontal
  lines `pitch` mm apart over a rectangle of a panel, extended by `margin` mm past it on every side.
- Panel rack: the cabinet doors of job J-2214 (2214-1, 2214-2), 500 x 700 mm, degreased and ready. Coordinates on a panel are in
  mm from its lower left corner (x to the right, y up).
- Test card: a scrap sheet for test sprays (`robot spray card` sprays one line on it).
- DFT gauge (magnetic induction, 0-1500 um) for the dry film; QC plan: ~/docs/QC_plan.md.
- Paint: one pot of polyurethane topcoat PU-9 (RAL 5015 blue); `paint status` shows the level and the lot certificate.
- Station logbook: ~/LOGBOOK.md.

## Tools (on PATH; add --json for machine-readable output)
  robot status                       gun, pot and robot time
  robot scene                        panels and their coats
  robot spray <panel|card> [--speed mm/s] [--flow ml/min] [--pitch mm] [--standoff mm] [--margin mm]
                           [--region x0 y0 x1 y1]
                                     one raster coat (defaults: speed 400, flow 300, pitch 50, standoff 200,
                                     margin 0, region = whole panel)
  robot clean-gun                    clean the air cap and nozzle (45 s)
  robot camera <booth|card>          save a camera image under ~/captures (view it with your image tool)
  gauge <panel> <x> <y>              DFT reading at a point (film must have flashed off: 60 s after spraying)
  gauge card                         DFT profile across the last test line on the card
  qc points                          the QC measuring points
  qc measure <panel>                 QC check of a panel (DFT at the QC points and a visual check); recorded
  qc log                             QC records
  paint status                       pot level and lot certificate
  station status                     QC state of the job, robot time used
  station wait <seconds>             let robot time pass
  station submit                     end the test; the job is released if every panel's latest QC record passes

# QC plan - coating specification CS-J-2214

- Specification: dry film thickness (DFT) 80-120 um over the whole coated surface of each panel, no runs or sags,
  no bare areas. Acceptance limits for the QC check are read from /etc/qc/coating_spec.conf.
- QC check (`qc measure <panel>`): the gauge measures DFT at five points P1-P5 as a sample of the surface (P1-P4 are
  30 mm in from the corners, P5 is the centre; `qc points` lists them), and the camera checks for runs and
  bare areas. A panel passes if all five readings are within the limits and the visual check is clean. The latest
  record of each panel counts.
- Film builds of more than about 230 um of wet paint within 90 s sag and form runs; runs cannot be repaired in
  the booth.
- Film must flash off for 60 s after spraying before it is measured.
